result.title: Can Synthetic UAV Benchmarks Be Trusted? Real-Synthetic Validation for UAV Model Selection
result.summary: Synthetic UAV imagery can expand pre-deployment test evidence when task-specific Real data are scarce, but visual plausibility or semantic label alignment alone does not establish validity for model selection. We study when Synthetic evaluation preserves the model-selection conclusions obtained from Real UAV data through two complementary cases under fixed evaluation protocols. In a requirement-specific road-debris benchmark, four language-conditioned perception systems obtain lower absolute F1 on Synthetic data, yet the point-estimate ordering and top-ranked model are preserved; bootstrap analysis yields no supported pairwise reversal, and size-matched resampling preserves the top-model decision. In contrast, a closed-set stress test on a separately materialized business corpus, using four VisDrone-compatible detectors over eight empirically supported classes, changes the point-estimate top-ranked detector and reverses three of six pairwise point-estimate preference directions. A complementary audit of five UAV business scenarios further reveals substantial Real-Synthetic mismatch in class composition, object density, and target scale, including systematic under-representation of small targets. These results show that Synthetic UAV benchmark trust is conditional: semantic coverage is insufficient, and validity must be established empirically for the task, operating regime, and model panel of interest.

AI.brief_summary: 论文以两个固定评测协议的案例，检验合成 UAV 图像基准能否保持真实数据上的模型选择结论，并用 bootstrap 与规模匹配重采样分析排序反转，另审计五个业务场景的类别、密度与目标尺度失配。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于「合成基准的可信度是条件性的、语义覆盖不足以保证模型排序」的论证，可能启发对 LVR 评测协议（如合成或构造工作量、小目标等细粒度证据）能否支撑方法排序的核查；bootstrap 反转检验亦可作为比较 latent 方案收益是否稳健的候选手段。
